chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Sa'dan, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Salih! When you carry a coffin, be as if you are the one being carried, and as if you asked your Lord for return to the world and He granted it, so look at what you would resume.'
He said, 'Then he said: I wonder at a people whose first ones are withheld from their last ones, then the call for departure is made among them while they are playing.'

key_terms.يَلْعَبُونَ: They are playing (engrossed in worldly affairs)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual perspective recommended when carrying a coffin in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises carrying the deceased with the perspective of one who has just died and is being asked to return to the world, prompting reflection on what one would resume doing. He further expresses wonder at those who are delayed in death while engrossed in worldly play, only to be called to depart suddenly. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a mirror for *hayat* (life), urging believers to treat death not as a distant event but as an imminent reality to ensure spiritual readiness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Sa’dan, from Ajlan Abu Salih who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Salih! Whenever you carry the coffin so become as if you are the carried one, and as if you are asking your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> for the return to the world and it is done. So look around, what is that which you would (like to) resume’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the people whose former ones have been withheld from (returning to) their later ones, then the departure is announced among them and they are playing’.
en.sarwar: 29. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Sa‘dan from ‘ Ajlan abu Salih who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘O abu Salih, when you help lift up someone’s coffin, consider it to be yourself being carried, as if you asked your Lord to give you a chance for returning back to the worldly life and your plea is granted. Think of how to live the new life. 5

The narrator has said that the Imam then said, ‘It is very odd indeed about the people whose predecessors are held back from returning to the present life and their successors are told to leave, but they are playfully unconcerned.
